opportunities.title: Front-door rebuild plus an after-hours intake agent that hands attorneys a ready-to-review matter summary
opportunities.problem: The firm has no machine-usable way for a client to reach it. The homepage renders with zero forms, zero inputs, zero iframes and zero tel: links; 'Contact' is an anchor into the About page; /contact/ serves homepage content; the only channels are two printed phone numbers, a fax and a personal Gmail address, and the firm's own site publishes no hours. Titles and site name still say 'Milltown' while the office is in North Brunswick, and the structured data carries only name, logo and a LinkedIn link - no address, phone or hours. A buyer who finds the firm at 8pm on a phone therefore has to dial a number nobody is answering, and an AI assistant or crawler has nothing to read or book.
evidence: Rendered DOM on the homepage has zero forms, zero inputs, zero iframes and zero tel: links; inquiry depends on two phone numbers, a fax number and a mailto: link to lozitolaw@gmail.com (https://lozitolaw.com/)

The /contact/ URL serves the homepage content with a canonical pointing at the homepage, so there is effectively no contact page, and the XML sitemap contains exactly two pages, home and about (https://lozitolaw.com/page-sitemap.xml)
Page title and Yoast site name still read 'Milltown, NJ' while the sitewide address block reads 480 Georges Rd, North Brunswick, NJ 08902 (https://lozitolaw.com/)

Structured data is a Yoast Organization/WebSite graph carrying name, logo and one LinkedIn sameAs - no address, phone, hours or legal-service schema; the only hours found anywhere are third-party (https://lozitolaw.com/about-lozito-law/)
The third-party aggregator profile with 83 reviews is flagged as not claimed by the business, leaving duplicate listing data unmanaged (https://reviews.birdeye.com/lozito-law-llc-155668563161464)
The firm markets remote closings via Remote Online Notarization, so it already serves clients it never meets in person - yet has no online intake path (https://lozitolaw.com/)

In a 2023 study of 1,300 US law firms' own web lead forms, 27% never responded at all and the median first response took 20 minutes among those that did (https://hennessey.com/2023-law-firm-lead-form-response-time-study/)
opportunities.agent_design: Two layers. (1) Rebuild the front door: a real /contact page with a multi-step intake form (matter type - residential purchase/sale, commercial, simple estate planning; property address; target closing date; whether a realtor or lender is involved; best way to reply), both office lines as tap-to-call links, published weekday hours, corrected copy that states the North Brunswick office honestly, and LegalService/LocalBusiness JSON-LD with address, phone, hours and areaServed so assistants and crawlers can read and cite the firm. Reconcile the Google Business Profile and the unclaimed Birdeye profile against the same source of truth, and configure NinjaFirewall so legitimate crawlers and the form endpoint are not 403'd. (2) Event-driven intake agent behind the form: on submission it acknowledges within seconds, asks 3-5 structured follow-ups (parties, lender, attorney-review date, who referred them), fills the fields the firm needs for a conflict check, drafts a one-page matter summary, writes it into the shared inbox/drive folder and pings both attorneys. The agent never quotes a fee, never gives legal advice and never accepts a matter: every enquiry sits in a 'pending attorney review' queue, and any client-facing message beyond the acknowledgement is sent only after a person approves it. Weekday-hours enquiries are routed to the office first, with the agent handling overflow and after-hours only.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A drag-and-drop form plugin produces a form, not a front door: it will not resolve the Milltown/North Brunswick entity confusion in titles and schema, will not reconcile three listings with different data, will not survive a WAF that already 403s automated clients, and will still leave after-hours enquiries unanswered. The agent layer needs qualification logic tied to the firm's accepted matter types, conflict-check fielding, reminder sequences and an approval gate, plus a zero-retention data path: enquiry content is prospective-client confidences under N.J. RPC 1.6, and supervision duties under RPC 5.3 mean each agent-drafted message needs an attributable reviewer.

impact_estimate.range: $4,000-$30,000 per year of flat-fee closing work recovered, plus removal of a documented discoverability gap
impact_estimate.assumptions: Inference, not measured for this firm: assume 1-3 enquiries a month currently arrive after 5pm or while both attorneys are on signings and are lost, and that only one in three of those converts. A NJ residential purchase/sale legal fee is typically quoted in the $1,000-$2,500 flat-fee range, so 1 enquiry/month at one-in-three conversion is roughly $4k-$10k/year and 3/month is roughly $12k-$30k/year. Excludes the value of the location mismatch fix and of being readable and bookable by AI assistants, which I have not priced. Does not assume any increase in total market demand.

opportunities.pilot_scope: Weeks 1-2: real contact page with the multi-step intake form, both tel: links, published hours, LegalService schema with address/phone/hours, corrected location copy, listing reconciliation checklist, and a firewall rule set that lets crawlers and the form through. Week 3: intake agent live behind an approval queue - acknowledgement, follow-up questions and a draft matter summary emailed to both attorneys. Week 4: measure enquiries captured by hour of day, time to first acknowledgement, and how many summaries an attorney accepted unchanged.

opportunities.title: Closing-file coordination agent: document chasing, milestone updates and signing scheduling per matter
opportunities.problem: Almost all of the firm's work is transactional closings, each one a repeatable checklist with several outside parties, and there is no system anywhere in the firm's footprint to run that checklist. The site has no client portal, no document upload, no checklist and no status page; the only channels are two phone lines and a Gmail mailbox. Reviews specifically praise the firm for keeping clients informed 'every step of the way', which is exactly the manual work that has to be done by hand today - by two attorneys and whatever support staff answer those two lines.
evidence: Practice areas listed are commercial real estate transactions, residential real estate transactions and simple estate planning - i.e. a volume of similar, checklist-driven files (https://lozitolaw.com/about-lozito-law/)

Two attorneys are profiled, Danielle M. Lozito, Esq. and Alyssa N. Seiden, Esq., with two published office lines and one fax; there is no client portal, booking widget, CRM embed or payment tool anywhere on the site (https://lozitolaw.com/about-lozito-law/)

Script inventory is limited to WordPress/Divi assets, jQuery, Yoast and a Google Analytics tag - no practice management or CRM embed, so file status lives in email and on disk (https://lozitolaw.com/)

Reviews repeatedly credit responsiveness and keeping clients informed through the closing, which implies substantial manual status-update correspondence per file (https://reviews.birdeye.com/lozito-law-llc-155668563161464)

Part of the closing workflow is already digital - signings can be orchestrated remotely via Remote Online Notarization - so the hand-off points an agent would touch exist today (https://lozitolaw.com/)

Legal-secretary work in this setting is defined by exactly these tasks: scheduling appointments, maintaining the attorney calendar, routing calls and assembling document sets (https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/43-6012.00)
opportunities.agent_design: A matter-scoped agent that opens a file when an attorney marks a new engagement and then runs the checklist: contract of sale and attorney-review letter, inspection reports, title commitment and clearance, mortgage commitment and lender conditions, closing disclosure, smoke/CO certificates, funds and final signing package. Triggers: an email arriving from a known party on the file, a document landing in the matter folder, or a date being reached. Actions: email the correct party for the one outstanding item (never a blast), chase on a defined cadence, post a short milestone update to buyer/seller/agent at each stage, propose two or three signing slots from the attorney's calendar, and prepare the RON packet for the appointment. Exceptions - missing title clearance, lender conditions, a party silent for more than N days, any date that would move a contractual deadline - are escalated to a named attorney and nothing proceeds without them. Every client-facing template is approved once by an attorney and then reused; the agent logs who was told what and when, which is the audit trail RPC 5.3 supervision calls for. Calendar commitments and any substantive legal statement stay attorney-only.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This is inbox-and-calendar orchestration across several outside parties, not conversation: it has to read unstructured lender and title emails, know which of eight documents on a file is still missing, hold state for weeks, and never move a contractual date on its own. Off-the-shelf chatbot subscriptions have no access to the firm's mail and drive, cannot schedule against an attorney's calendar, and have no approval queue or per-file audit log. Confidentiality (RPC 1.6) rules out pasting contract and settlement content into consumer endpoints; the deployment has to be tenant-isolated with a DPA.

impact_estimate.range: roughly 15-90 staff hours per month, i.e. $9,000-$35,000 per year of support capacity at NJ legal-secretary pay, before any throughput gain
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes 15-30 active closings a month (inference - no file volume is published) at 1-3 staff hours saved each for document chasing, status updates and scheduling; hourly cost derived from the NJ legal-secretary and administrative-assistant median of $63,080 per year, about $30/hour before benefits. The lower bound assumes only chasing and status email are automated; the upper bound also assumes scheduling and RON packet prep. Market per-matter savings figures are mostly vendor case studies, so I have not used them; treat this as capacity freed, which converts to margin only if it reduces write-downs or raises matter volume.

opportunities.pilot_scope: Run on two live residential files end to end for three weeks: auto-generated per-file checklist, automated requests and chases for outstanding documents, milestone update emails from approved templates, and proposed signing slots in the attorney's calendar. Deliverable is a before/after time log per file, the exception log, and a decision on which steps deserve autonomy versus approval.

opportunities.title: Firm knowledge agent: attorney-approved answer bank built from the firm's own checklist, engagement letters and closing documents
opportunities.problem: There is no written body of answers anywhere the firm or its clients can consult: no FAQ, no document checklist, no downloadable 'what to bring to closing', no service pages, only two pages total. So every recurring question - when do I get the title commitment, what is attorney review, which documents do I send, what happens at signing, can we sign remotely - is answered live, on one of two phone lines, by someone who is also closing deals. The same gap applies internally: a new or temporary assistant has no playbook to read because the playbook is in the attorneys' heads.
evidence: No blog, no FAQ, no case results, no downloadable checklist or document list and no pricing content; the sitemap has two URLs in total (https://lozitolaw.com/page-sitemap.xml)
The About page has not changed since May 2023 and the site's only content is prose and photos, so nothing on the web answers a client's procedural questions (https://lozitolaw.com/page-sitemap.xml)
Client contact runs through two phone numbers and one Gmail address, with no form or chat, so all question-answering is human and synchronous (https://lozitolaw.com/about-lozito-law/)

Reviews reference helpful office staff handling client contact, implying non-attorney staff answer these questions with no written knowledge base (https://reviews.birdeye.com/lozito-law-llc-155668563161464)

Asked verifiable questions about random federal court cases, ChatGPT-4 produced legal hallucinations about 58% of the time - peer-reviewed in Journal of Legal Analysis 16(1), 2024 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.01301)

A preregistered academic working paper (not peer-reviewed) found commercial RAG legal tools from Lexis and Westlaw still hallucinated 17-33% of the time, so retrieval alone does not earn autonomy (https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.20362)

Error consequence is graded high in this occupation: 50% of lawyers rate 'consequence of error' extremely serious and 60% rate being exact or accurate extremely important (https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/23-1011.00)
opportunities.agent_design: Start with a one-time capture: the agent interviews the attorneys to extract the firm's actual closing sequence, document list, RON procedure and estate-planning intake, and drafts the playbook, which the attorneys correct and sign off. That signed-off playbook plus the firm's engagement letters and standard forms become the only retrieval corpus - the agent answers strictly from those documents, quotes the passage it used, and returns 'not covered, ask the attorney' rather than reasoning from general law. Two surfaces: (a) internal - staff ask 'what is outstanding on this file' or 'what do we send a seller before closing' and get a cited answer, with unanswered questions logged into a weekly gap list the attorneys close; (b) client-facing - a public FAQ and document checklist generated from answers an attorney has explicitly approved, plus a short self-serve status page fed by the closing agent's milestone data. Deployed tenant-isolated with zero-retention settings because the corpus and questions touch client confidences; no client name, address or document content is used to train anything.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A general chatbot answering legal-procedure questions is the exact failure mode the evidence describes - a 58% hallucination rate on verifiable legal questions, and 17-33% even in purpose-built legal research tools - so the design has to be closed-book retrieval from the firm's own signed-off documents with a hard 'no source, no answer' rule and attorney approval of the answer bank. That requires document ingestion with permissions mirroring the firm's drive, per-answer provenance an attorney can audit, an unanswered-question log, and a private deployment because of RPC 1.6. None of that is available from a subscription chatbot, and RPC 1.1 competence plus RPC 5.3 supervision make an unaudited answer the firm's liability.

impact_estimate.range: roughly 2-5 staff hours a week returned, i.e. $3,000-$8,000 per year, plus a written playbook the firm does not have today
impact_estimate.assumptions: Inference: assumes 3-8 repetitive status/FAQ contacts a day across two lines (no call volume is published) and that half of them become self-serve or are handled in one pass with a cited answer; valued at the NJ legal-secretary median of $63,080, about $30/hour, at 2-5 hours a week. Deliberately does not double-count the closing agent's document chasing - this estimate covers question answering only. Client-experience benefit (fewer 'nobody told me' complaints) is not priced.

opportunities.pilot_scope: Weeks 1-2: structured interviews with both attorneys to draft the closing and estate-planning playbook; attorneys mark it up and sign it off. Week 3: internal-only Q&A agent over that playbook plus engagement letters, with citation display and an unanswered-question log. Week 4: publish the subset of answers the attorneys approved as a public FAQ and document checklist, and report the log of questions the corpus could not answer.

lead_score.rationale: Pain is unusually well evidenced for the front door: zero forms, zero tel: links, no real contact page, no published hours, the Milltown/North Brunswick mismatch, an unclaimed aggregator listing and an Organization-only schema were all verified directly in HTML, the sitemap, robots.txt and the Google panel, not inferred. The operational pain (lost after-hours enquiries, manual closing coordination, undocumented playbook) is inference from practice type and review themes - the firm publishes no file volume, headcount or complaint, so those estimates are ranges only. Fit is good for G, A and C but partial for the rest: no inventory, fleet or shop floor, so no physical/edge opportunity is proposed - no avenues.json was supplied, and a two-attorney office with a single meeting room has nothing for cameras or sensors to measure; capability E is consciously excluded, not overlooked. Ability to pay is the weak sub-score: two attorneys, one office, a flat-fee closing model and a marketing footprint untouched since 2023 suggest a small referral-driven budget, and NJ lawyer pay benchmarks (median $161,430 statewide) are not a proxy for firm cash. Ease is strong on scope - one decision maker, WordPress, no legacy integrations - but reduced by a firewall that 403s automated clients, a consumer Gmail rather than a domain mailbox, no practice management system to integrate with, and mandatory attorney approval on every client-facing message. Strategic value is the main argument: the same brochure-only firm with no intake path exists in every NJ town, and closing coordination is a repeatable vertical play re-sellable with one checklist template. Suggested sequence: front door and intake agent first (fixed-fee, fast, visible), then the closing coordination agent, then the knowledge agent once the playbook exists - they compound, since the playbook and the milestone data feed each other.

best_evidence_signal: The firm's homepage renders with zero forms, zero inputs and zero tel: links and its /contact/ URL serves the homepage, so a client's only route in is a printed phone number or a Gmail address (https://lozitolaw.com/)
